questions.stem: A crane is described as being "abaft the beam". Where is it?
options: Toward the bow from the widest point of the ship
Toward the stern from the widest point of the ship
On the centreline, directly over the keel of the ship
Outside the hull, hanging over the side at the waterline
questions.explanation: Abaft means toward the stern relative to some object or point. Here the point is the beam (the widest part), so abaft the beam is behind it, toward the stern. Toward the bow would be "forward of the beam".

options: Fore and aft, along the full length of the ship
Side to side, at right angles to the centreline
Toward the bow, forward of the widest part of the hull
Halfway along the ship, at the midpoint of her length
questions.explanation: Athwartships is across the ship at right angles to the fore-and-aft centreline. Along the ship is fore and aft; halfway along is amidships.

options: Outboard: toward the centreline; inboard: outside the hull of the ship
Amidships: right at the stern; aft: halfway along the length of the ship
Beam: width at the widest point; amidships: halfway along the length
Port: the right side looking forward; starboard: the left side looking forward
questions.explanation: Beam is the maximum width and amidships is the middle. Outboard and inboard are the wrong way round in the first option, aft and amidships are confused in the second, and port is the left side, not the right.

questions.stem: A fitting must withstand water pressure from both sides of the door or hatch. Which word describes it?
options: Weathertight
Watertight
Splash-proof
Deck-proof
questions.explanation: Watertight fittings must resist pressure from either side. Weathertight fittings only need to resist pressure from the outside, enough to keep water out in any sea conditions. The other two words are not standard terms.

options: In any sea conditions, water will not penetrate into the ship
Water cannot pass in either direction even at full flooding pressure
Rain will not enter in light weather only
The door is permanently welded shut
questions.explanation: The Load Lines convention wording is that in any sea conditions water will not penetrate into the ship. Resisting pressure from both directions describes watertight, not weathertight.

questions.stem: Which statement about bitts and bollards is right?
options: A bollard is only fitted ashore; bitts are only fitted on aircraft carriers
Bitts and bollards are both posts on which lines are made fast
A bollard is a pair of horizontal drums used for lifting cargo aboard
Bitts and fairleads are the same fitting under two different names
questions.explanation: Both are posts to which lines are secured: bitts are a post or pair of posts, and a bollard is a substantial vertical pillar. A fairlead is a different fitting that guides a line, and cargo lifting is done by derricks or cranes.

options: A portable flight of steps down the side of a ship
A fixed steel ladder running down inside a cargo hold
A rope ladder hung from a mast for going aloft
A short ladder fitted in the crew's sleeping cabins
questions.explanation: An accommodation ladder is a portable flight of steps down the ship's side, used for boarding from a boat or the quay. It is not the same as a rope or pilot ladder, nor a ladder inside the ship.

questions.stem: The bosun says: "Stow the fenders outboard of the rail, starboard side, abaft the accommodation." Where do the fenders go?
options: Inside the rail on the left side, toward the bow from the accommodation
Outside the rail, right side, toward the stern from the accommodation
On the centreline of the deck, close behind the accommodation block
Outside the rail on the right side, toward the bow from the accommodation
questions.explanation: Outboard of the rail means outside it; starboard is the right side looking forward; abaft the accommodation means toward the stern from it. The other options get one of these three words wrong.

questions.stem: In which sense does "aft" differ from "abaft"?
options: They are exact synonyms and can always be swapped freely
Aft is a general direction; abaft is relative to an object
Abaft means toward the bow, aft means toward the stern
Aft is a word used only for aircraft, abaft only for ships
questions.explanation: Aft is toward the stern in general. Abaft needs a reference object (abaft the beam, abaft the funnel). Toward the bow is forward or fore.
